newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate falls, baht rises late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate falls, baht rises late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate dropped to 9.00-9.50 percent in late trade on Wednesday from 11.00-11.25 percent early on higher liquiditiy, dealers said.

"Banks and finance companies appeared to have a lot of excess fund today. The interbank rate is likely to ease further despite the central bank's reserve deadline on Friday," said one dealer at a local bank.
Dealers said the rising liquidity was attributed to heavy selling of the dollar in the foreign exchange market and falling dollar/baht swap premiums.
The baht strengthened to 25.407-25.412 to the dollar in late trade from 25.427-25.431 early as the U.S. unit's weakness abroad encouraged stop-loss dollar selling here, dealers said.
"There was heavy dollar selling today following the U.S. unit's sharp fall against the major currencies," said one currency dealer.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was lower to 8.50/9.25 satangs per dollar late against 9.00/9.50 in the morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.43 to the dollar against 25.42 on Tuesday.
